free_tier.stated: No free tier. VPS - NAT512 is USD 7.50 a year, printed '$7.5 / year', for 512 MB RAM, 5 GB SSD, 1 fair-use CPU core, a /80 IPv6 plus NAT IPv4 and 750 GB a month.

retention.stated: annual prepay; no deletion interval after expiry was published on the pages read. The terms disclaim all warranties and limit damages to 'the immediate termination of service'.

egress.terms: 750 GB a month on NAT512, printed '750GB transfer per month'

interface_detail: KVM guest with root, a /80 IPv6 subnet plus NAT IPv4 with 20 usable ports and one SSH port, across France, Canada, the Netherlands, Norway, New York, Los Angeles, Singapore and Japan
tooling: any SSH client; a WHMCS portal at clients.natvps.net; the vendor publishes an IPv4 port calculator
chaining: a 512 MB KVM box with a /80 and 21 ports at USD 0.625 a month, from a vendor whose own FAQ says WireGuard and OpenVPN are supported, and which names no legal entity anywhere

limits.value: 20 usable ports plus 1 SSH port on the shared IPv4, plus a /80 IPv6 subnet

binding_note: 21 ports is a workable budget but they are shared-IP ports on a /80 rather than a /64, and the vendor names no legal entity, so the risk sits with the seller rather than the quota.

identity_cost.detail: the cart requires a login before it prices anything: the order page states 'Your cart is empty' and shows a sign-in form with 'Email Address', 'Password' and 'Image Verification'. The registration page at ?/register/ returns 404, so account creation happens at checkout and the field list could not be read. Payment rails and any authorisation hold are unestablished. No national ID requirement is published anywhere read.

reliability_note: the vendor publishes a status page at status.natvps.net showing node health, with 'Canada [CAN-K2]' at 100 percent when read; the terms disclaim all warranties and cap damages at termination of service; no SLA published
confidence_note: price, shape, the /80, the port count, the traffic and the vendor's own WireGuard statement are quoted from the vendor's own pages read; the login gate on the cart is quoted from the cart page. Not documented: the checkout fields, the payment rails and the legal entity, which is named nowhere.

evidence.proved: quoted plan: 'VPS - NAT512 $7.5 / year 512MB RAM 5GB SSD disk space 1 CPU Core (fair use) /80 IPv6 + NAT IPv4 750GB transfer per month' with the order link to clients.natvps.net/?/cart/nat-vps--kvm-/

quoted port and protocol answer: 'Yes you can! We include 20 usable ports + 1 SSH port for IPv4 access.' and 'Create your own private VPN - most methods including OpenVPN & Wireguard can be used. Dual stack IPv4+IPv6 connectivity.'
quoted second tier: 'VPS - NAT768 $10 / year 768MB RAM 7GB SSD disk space 1 CPU Core (fair use) /80 IPv6 + NAT IPv4 1024GB transfer per month'

the cart did not price anything without an account: the page reads 'Your cart is empty Browse Products and Services' and renders a sign-in form with 'Email Address', 'Password' and 'Image Verification'. It also warns 'Turn off your VPN before placing an order'.
no standalone registration page exists: the route answers '404 Not Found - Sorry, an error has occurred, Requested page not found!'

the terms name no company: the text refers only to 'NatVPS' throughout and states 'NatVPS specifically disclaims all warranties for merchant ability and fitness for a particular purpose' with damages limited to 'the immediate termination of service'
a status page exists and lists nodes, reading 'Canada [CAN-K2]' at '100%' when fetched

notes: And no legal entity is named anywhere: the terms refer only to 'NatVPS', there is no company name, number or address on any page read, and the footer carries a Discord invite where an entity would normally sit. That is not the dissolved-company trap, but it is the same absence of a party to hold responsible, and for an annual prepay it belongs in the record rather than in a footnote. The cart could not price the plan: the order route requires a login and shows 'Your cart is empty', and there is no standalone registration page, so the checkout fields and the payment rails are unestablished. The stock position is also not published anywhere on the marketing page; only the status page gives node health.
